questions.prompt: A 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1 is half of an equilateral triangle with side 1. Which derivation of sin(π/3) and cos(π/3) is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: A 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1 is half of an equilateral triangle with side 1. Which derivation of sin(π/3) and cos(π/3) is correct?

choices.text: The short leg is 1/2 and the long leg is √(1 - 1/4) = √3/2. The angle π/3 is opposite the long leg, so sin(π/3) = √3/2 and cos(π/3) = 1/2.
The long leg is √(1 + 1/4) = √5/2, so sin(π/3) = √5/2.
The short leg is 1/2 and the long leg is √(1 - 1/4) = √3/2. The angle π/3 is opposite the short leg, so sin(π/3) = 1/2 and cos(π/3) = √3/2.
The legs are 1/2 and 1 - 1/2 = 1/2, so sin(π/3) = cos(π/3) = 1/2.

questions.correct_answer: The short leg is 1/2 and the long leg is √(1 - 1/4) = √3/2. The angle π/3 is opposite the long leg, so sin(π/3) = √3/2 and cos(π/3) = 1/2.
questions.grading_note: Halving the base gives 1/2; the Pythagorean Theorem gives √3/2; the larger angle is opposite the longer leg. The others put π/3 opposite the short leg, subtract lengths instead of using the Pythagorean Theorem, or add instead of subtracting squares.

questions.prompt: Which derivation of tan(π/6) from a special triangle is correct?

choices.text: The opposite side is half the hypotenuse, so tan(π/6) = 1/2.
In the 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1, π/6 is opposite the leg 1/2 and adjacent to the leg √3/2, so tan(π/6) = (1/2)/(√3/2) = 1/√3 = √3/3.
In the 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1, π/6 is opposite the leg √3/2 and adjacent to the leg 1/2, so tan(π/6) = (√3/2)/(1/2) = √3 exactly.

questions.correct_answer: In the 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1, π/6 is opposite the leg 1/2 and adjacent to the leg √3/2, so tan(π/6) = (1/2)/(√3/2) = 1/√3 = √3/3.
questions.grading_note: Opposite over adjacent, then simplify (1/2)/(√3/2) = 1/√3 = √3/3. The others use the angle π/3, give sin(π/6) instead, or simplify the quotient incorrectly.
